title: After a car crash: what to do first
metaDesc: In a crash? Stop, call 911 if anyone is hurt, get off the road if you can, and swap information. What to do next and when you have to report it.
first: Stop. You must stop after any crash, even a small one.
Call 911 if anyone is hurt or might be hurt.
If no one is hurt and the car can move, move it off the road. Turn on your hazard lights.
If the airbags went off, don't drive the car. Have it towed.
Swap information with the other driver: names, addresses, license numbers, plates, and insurance company and policy number.
dont: Don't leave the scene. Leaving after a crash breaks the law, and it's a crime if anyone is hurt.
Don't move someone who is hurt unless there's fire or another danger right now.
Stay away from downed power lines. If one touches your car, stay inside until help comes.
Keep flares away from any leaking fuel.

steps.t: Hazard lights on. If it's safe, set out reflectors or flares behind the cars to warn other drivers, but not near leaking fuel. Wait somewhere away from traffic.
Call 911 if anyone is hurt. Say where you are and how many people are hurt, and make sure an ambulance is coming. In some states, like California, you call 911 to report any crash.

Give the other driver your name, address, driver's license number, registration, and insurance company, policy number and dates. Get the same from them, plus their plate number. Write it down or take photos if it's safe.

steps.h: Hit a parked car or something else?
steps.t: Try to find the owner. If you can't, leave a note with your name and address on the car, and report it to the police.
A crash hard enough to set off the airbags can damage parts you can't see. Don't drive the car. Have it towed and checked.

steps.h: Report it if your state says so
steps.t: Many states make you report some crashes to the DMV, often within days. New York and California both want a report within 10 days if anyone is hurt or the damage is above a set amount. In New York, telling your insurance company doesn't count as reporting to the DMV. Check your state DMV's website.
Call a parent, guardian or the car's owner. Let the insurance company know soon.

call: Call 911 if anyone is hurt or might be hurt, there's smoke or fire, or the cars are blocking traffic.
For a tow, call your roadside plan or your insurer's roadside line.
